name: Technology and Core Infrastructure
blurb: What AI is built from: the models themselves, the silicon and datacenters they run on, the APIs and datasets that feed them, and the languages, frameworks, agents, and protocols developers use to build with them.

domains.name: Foundation Models
domains.blurb: Every released model, by modality and purpose, with full release, licence, architecture, context, pricing, performance, and safety metadata.

sections.name: Large Language Models
sections.blurb: General purpose text models, by family, size, and licence.

sections.name: Reasoning Models
sections.blurb: Models trained or tuned to work through problems step by step before answering.

sections.name: Multimodal Models
sections.blurb: Models that accept and produce more than one modality.

sections.name: Vision Models
sections.blurb: Image understanding, detection, segmentation, and document vision.

sections.name: Image Generation Models
sections.blurb: Text to image and image editing models.

sections.name: Video Models
sections.blurb: Video generation, understanding, and editing.

sections.name: Audio and Speech Models
sections.blurb: Speech recognition, synthesis, and audio understanding.

sections.name: Music Models
sections.blurb: Music generation and audio composition.

sections.name: Embedding Models
sections.blurb: Vector representations for search, clustering, and retrieval.

sections.name: OCR and Translation Models
sections.blurb: Document extraction and machine translation.

sections.name: Coding Models
sections.blurb: Models trained for code generation, review, and repair. Membership is the Hub's own code tag on text-generation models, ranked by all-time downloads.

sections.name: Small Language Models
sections.blurb: Compact models that trade capability for cost and latency. The cut is a declared parameter count of four billion or fewer from safetensors metadata; models that do not publish a count cannot appear.

sections.name: On-device and Edge Models
sections.blurb: Models packaged to run on phones, laptops, and embedded hardware. Membership is the GGUF tag, the format llama.cpp and most local runtimes load, ranked by downloads.

sections.name: Robotics Models
sections.blurb: Vision-language-action and control models for physical systems.

sections.name: Scientific Models
sections.blurb: Models for chemistry and biology: molecular property prediction, protein language models, and scientific NER. Membership is the Hub's chemistry and biology tags.

sections.name: Medical Models
sections.blurb: Clinical, imaging, and biomedical models, by the Hub's medical tag. Reference material about models, not medical advice.

sections.name: Legal Models
sections.blurb: Models tuned for legal text: contracts, statutes, and case language, by the Hub's legal tag. Reference material about models, not legal advice.

sections.name: Financial Models
sections.blurb: Models tuned for financial text and market language, by the Hub's finance tag. Reference material about models, not investment advice.

sections.name: Model Metadata Standard
sections.blurb: The full record kept for every model: release and licence, parameters and architecture, context and training data, distribution, pricing and performance, and safety.

domains.name: AI Infrastructure and Hardware
domains.blurb: GPUs, NPUs, TPUs, chip fabs, memory and storage, plus the datacenters, power, cooling, and networking underneath them.

sections.name: GPUs
sections.blurb: Datacenter and workstation GPUs, by generation, memory, and throughput.

sections.name: NPUs and TPUs
sections.blurb: Purpose-built accelerators outside the GPU line.

sections.name: Chip Fabrication
sections.blurb: This section covers the companies that physically manufacture AI silicon, on which process nodes, and where.

sections.name: Memory and Storage
sections.blurb: This section covers the memory that sits next to the accelerator and the storage tiers that keep it fed.

sections.name: Memory Supply
sections.blurb: Who makes the memory on an AI accelerator, why no index tracks its price, how it drives up PC memory prices, and how HBM4 changes the chip.

sections.name: Networking Fabric
sections.blurb: This section covers the interconnect inside and between training nodes: the scale-up fabric that links GPUs within a rack and the scale-out fabric that links racks into a cluster.

domains.name: AI APIs and Integrations
domains.blurb: Endpoints, SDKs, authentication, rate limits, pricing, uptime, and changelogs for every public AI API.

sections.name: API Directory
sections.blurb: Every public AI API with endpoints, SDKs, and authentication.

sections.name: API Pricing
sections.blurb: Rates, rate limits, and how billing actually works per provider.

sections.name: Model Serving Providers
sections.blurb: The companies that actually run the inference behind AI model APIs: 100+ serving providers with headquarters country, datacenter regions, and links to each one's terms of service, privacy policy, and live status page.

sections.name: API Status and Uptime
sections.blurb: Reliability history and changelogs.

domains.name: AI Datasets
domains.blurb: Training and evaluation datasets with size, licence, provenance, language coverage, and documented bias.

sections.name: Training Datasets
sections.blurb: Corpora used to pre-train models, with provenance and licence.

sections.name: Evaluation Datasets
sections.blurb: Benchmarks and test sets, and what each actually measures.

sections.name: Dataset Licensing and Provenance
sections.blurb: What may lawfully be used for what, and how to tell.

domains.name: Data Centers
domains.blurb: The physical ledger of the AI boom: builder capital expenditure from SEC filings, a national facility registry, grid and power metrics, and the nuclear programs racing to feed the next gigawatt of compute.

sections.name: The Genesis Mission
sections.blurb: The Department of Energy's national AI for science programme: the executive order, the $5 billion expansion, 278 projects, and the companies supplying the compute.

domains.name: Programming Languages and Frameworks
domains.blurb: The languages AI is written in and the frameworks built on top of them, tracked by adoption, releases, licence, and integrations.

sections.name: Programming Languages
sections.blurb: Python, Rust, C++, Mojo, and Julia in AI work.

sections.name: AI Frameworks
sections.blurb: LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy, Semantic Kernel, and the rest.

sections.name: Inference Engines
sections.blurb: vLLM, TensorRT, llama.cpp, and the serving layer.

domains.name: AI Agents and the MCP Ecosystem
domains.blurb: Autonomous and multi-agent systems, planning and memory, tool use, and the Model Context Protocol servers, clients, registries, and security model.

sections.name: Autonomous Agents
sections.blurb: This section covers single agents that take a goal and run their own loop of planning, tool calls, and self-correction without a person approving each step.

sections.name: Multi-agent Systems
sections.blurb: This section covers what happens when more than one agent is involved: orchestration frameworks that run a set of agents, delegation patterns that hand work between them, and the wire protocols agents from different vendors use to talk to each other.

sections.name: Agent Memory and Planning
sections.blurb: This section covers the layer that lets an agent carry state across turns and across sessions: storing what happened, retrieving the relevant part of it later, and building the working context an agent plans against.

sections.name: Coding and Browser Agents
sections.blurb: This section covers agents that operate a real tool rather than only producing text: agents that read and edit a codebase and run its tests, and agents that drive a browser by clicking, typing, and reading pages.

sections.name: Voice and Service Agents
sections.blurb: This section covers agents that hold a spoken conversation in real time: the frameworks that stitch together speech recognition, a model, speech synthesis, and a telephony or WebRTC transport tight enough that a caller does not hear the seams.

sections.name: MCP Servers
sections.blurb: Every active server in the official Model Context Protocol registry: who publishes it, what it exposes, whether it is hosted or runs locally, and where to get it.

sections.name: MCP Clients
sections.blurb: Applications that speak MCP.

sections.name: MCP SDKs and Registries
sections.blurb: The tooling and directories around the protocol.

sections.name: MCP Security and Authentication
sections.blurb: Trust boundaries, credentials, and the failure modes.

sections.name: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol
sections.blurb: The open standard for agent-to-agent delegation: Agent Cards, task lifecycle, three protocol bindings, enterprise auth schemes, and how it complements MCP. Google-originated, Linux Foundation-governed, verified from the v1.0 specification.

sections.name: Vibe Coding
sections.blurb: Building by describing intent while the model writes the code: what the term covers, where a project sits on the spectrum from throwaway prototype to agentic production workflow, the conventions agents read, and a map to everything else on...
